caption:
With kimonos, cheap T-Shirts and some bins it was really refreshing to come across a thrift store in Japan that still feels like ‘in the trenches’ thrifting and not just curated items. That being said they also had some really cool vintage pieces in the back so it was a good balance of everything! Definitely check out @wa_store_kyoto if you’re looking for a Kyoto thrift shop! 

Location: 337 Iseyacho, Nakagyo Ward, Kyoto, 604-8066

#tokyo #kyoto #japan #kyotothriftshop #thrift #japanthrift #thrifting #japanfashion #kyotofashion #tokyofashion".
transcription: This is one of Kyoto's best thrift stores. With shirts as low as 70 cents, some of the funky's t-shirts and even old kimonos, it was refreshing to come across a store that's less $7 bins and not just curated item. Apparently they consistently have sales on their brand name pickups and vintage items, not to mention my favorite niche t-shirt. But I do have to give in honorable mentions these really cool football kits and these baskets full of 30 to 40 year old pins from France. There's a lot to find here, so it's definitely worth stopping by if you're in Kyoto. Okay, so I picked up this Kamo T and this really cool brand open, but I honestly, I regret not getting the pregnancy t-shirt, so someone's gotta go grab that before it's gone.

caption:
Tucked away near Meidaimae Station in Setagaya, Miles is one of Tokyo’s oldest and most beloved jazz kissaten, quietly echoing the Showa era since it first opened in 1960.

With just around 10 seats, Miles offers an intimate setting where regulars and newcomers sit shoulder to shoulder, immersing themselves in classic jazz grooves. It is said that John Coltrane stopped by during his visit to Japan in 1966.

If you’re longing for a time‑slowed moment in Tokyo— Miles is your sanctuary. Be sure to stop by, quietly request a favorite record, and experience the timeless magic of Tokyo’s kissaten culture. Save this one for your next visit!
